prompt: Mid-case: Delivery times rose from 3 to 5 days. You've found that warehouse processing takes 2 extra days since a new system launched in March, and that carrier transit time is unchanged. You also learned the carrier rebranded in May. You haven't looked at staffing. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: the 2 extra days come from warehouse processing since the March system launch; carrier transit is unchanged. Next I'd check staffing.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open.

options.text: So far: the new system caused the 2-day delay, so the fix is to roll it back before the busy season.
options.feedback: It jumps to a fix before checking staffing, which could have changed at the same time.

options.text: So far: warehouse processing and carrier transit both slowed, adding 2 days between them. Staffing comes next.
options.feedback: It misstates what you found: carrier transit is unchanged.

options.text: So far: warehouse processing added 2 days after the March system launch, and the carrier rebranded in May. Next, staffing.
options.feedback: The carrier's rebrand has nothing to do with the delay, so it doesn't belong in the summary.

explanation: Known: warehouse processing added 2 days after the March system launch; carrier transit is unchanged. Suspected: the new system. Next: check staffing. If staffing also changed in March, the system may not be the whole cause.
